newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Kinkel talks in Moscow, NATO differences remain.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel talks in Moscow, NATO differences remain.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel took the West's case for NATO enlargement to Moscow on Tuesday but there was little sign the two sides were getting much closer on the issue after his first day of talks.

"There are differences of opinion," Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov told a joint news conference after a two-hour meeting with his German counterpart. "Russia will always have a negative attitude towards (NATO) enlargement."

Kinkel said that, in talks with Primakov and President Boris Yeltsin's chief-of-staff, Anatoly Chubais, he had repeated the West's offer of a "special charter" for Russia with the western defence alliance. But, he said, differences remained over NATO's plans to admit former Soviet-bloc states in eastern Europe.

Both Primakov and Chubais repeated Moscow's insistence on a "legally binding" agreement with NATO, granting Russia a big formal say in an alliance whose expansion the Kremlin sees as a threat and a political embarrassment in the face of mounting attacks on the ailing Yeltsin by nationalist opponents.

Western leaders, whose diplomatic offensive will be followed up this week by Italian Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini and new U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright, are reluctant to mire plans for expansion in complex legal wrangling.
They hope to invite new members, possibly Poland, Hungary or the Czech Republic, after a summit in Madrid in July.
"I hope that we manage to reach an agreement by the NATO summit so that the summit can be held in a way that would satisfy both sides," Kinkel said.
Chubais, he said, expressed a similar hope.
Primakov told the news conference: "We're ready to talk about ways to relieve our concern and ways of reaching an agreement that satisfies all sides."

But the minister, who meets NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana in Brussels on Monday, added: "We will only be satisfied with a legally binding agreement, whatever that may be...Many charters have been signed and then forgotten."
Kinkel is due to have talks with Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Wednesday before flying home.

He said he also expected to talk to Yeltsin by telephone during the day. The president is recovering at a country residence near Moscow from the pneumonia which disrupted his convalescence from a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5.

Kinkel met Albright in Bonn this week. Washington's new diplomatic chief is touring European capitals trying to ensure a united front within NATO (North Atlantic Treaty Organisation) before she holds talks with Yeltsin in Moscow on Friday.
